doc.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The big band, Kogun and Japanese color
title: Touring without noh players: the prerecorded tape
summary: She used a tape, except for Carnegie Hall and a Japanese hall with real players.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: So when you make the recording, but how can you tour this? You have to take these artists with you to tour, to tour, to recreate this piece when you‟re touring.

But twice we had real players, in Japan. That was a luxury. And also here at the concert … uh, uh … the one time was at Carnegie Hall [recorded and released as Carnegie Hall Concert by Columbia in 1991], and then another time at Sankei Hall in Japan, they had a real player. But most of the time, for example, we used to play every Monday night at Birdland in New York, and every Monday night, and I had a tape recorder set for that and prerecorded. So, yeah, that‟s … you know, if you are a classical organization, you can afford to have, their budget will provide it, even though it‟s like a twenty-minute piece of music and all you need is one note [chuckles], they will, that musician was hired. We don‟t have that kind of luxury, so….
